title: Sonnental teaser brings the Dark team back to German mysteries
body_md:
HBO Max has released the first teaser for Sonnental, a German mystery thriller associated with Dark creators Jantje Friese and Baran bo Odar. The report published on November 26, 2026, highlights a return to the unsettling woodland atmosphere familiar to viewers of their Netflix hit. Lisa Vicari, another familiar face from Dark, leads the new six-part series.

Vicari plays Anja Vogler, a criminal profiler who returns to her hometown to investigate a murder. As the investigation develops and additional victims are discovered, she begins to identify connections between the crimes and motifs from Struwwelpeter, a real German children's book. Its cautionary stories use disturbing consequences to warn children against misbehavior.

The literary inspiration offers the series a distinctive foundation for its mystery. Childhood memories and familiar cultural imagery can acquire threatening meanings when they become connected to a criminal investigation. Anja's return home also creates opportunities to explore the relationship between her professional responsibilities and personal history. The available description does not establish whether the story includes supernatural phenomena, and similarities to Dark should not be taken as evidence of time travel or a comparable narrative structure.

Peter Kurth, known for Babylon Berlin, plays investigator Norbert Troschitz. Jan Friedrichsen appears as Anja's son Max, while Iris Böhm portrays her mother Kerstin. The regular cast also includes Merlin Rose, Maria Simon, Mišel Matičević and Stipe Erceg.

An important distinction concerns the project's creative credits. Although the report connects Sonnental with Friese and bo Odar, it identifies Matija Dragojević as the series creator. Dragojević co-wrote the project with Bob Konrad, whose previous credits include Kleo and 4 Blocks. The new series should therefore not be described as having been created exclusively by the team behind Dark.

Dark ran for three seasons between 2017 and 2020, building an international audience through its complex storytelling and ominous atmosphere. Friese and bo Odar subsequently worked on the period mystery 1899, which Netflix canceled after one season. A new German-language thriller connected to the pair is consequently likely to attract interest from viewers who followed those earlier projects.

Sonnental is scheduled to release all six episodes on HBO Max in March 2027. The report does not specify an exact premiere day. Until further footage or details become available, the central attraction is the combination of a hometown investigation, a disturbing literary reference and a cast that reconnects audiences with the world of German mystery television.
